title: Trust gates before reading a test: split check, significant read, guardrails
decision_task: May ClimbOS read or report an effect from this split test yet? / Can a recorded outcome say the change caused extra conversions? / Did the change cause harm that blocks shipping, and may the test stop early for it?
business_types: any business running a split test
applies_when: ab_split or holdout with a planned allocation
owner, integration or ad tool reports per-arm counts
any live test touching customers: email, offers, pricing, booking flow, ads
exclusions: before/after or observational designs (no planned split)
platform-run tests that do not expose per-arm counts (label attributed)
SRM failed or warned and unresolved
required_inputs: same unit counted in both arms
evidence_requirements: observed units per arm at the analysis date
1-3 guardrails each with a numeric bound written before launch
missing_data_behavior: Per-arm counts unknown: no effect read; label 'attributed' if a platform reports it.
Planned split unknown: ask before any read.
No guardrails set: the test can't be marked 'met'.
alternatives_when_constrained: low traffic: switch to alternating weeks or a before/after labelled observational
no instrumentation: manual tally of sends per arm before any outcome count
low traffic: report as directional with the interval of plausible changes
no instrumentation: not_run or owner tally labelled observed
low traffic: absolute bounds with a minimum count instead of significance
no randomization: compare guardrail to the pre-period, labelled observed

decision_branches.then: Block 'met'; harm stops are allowed early.

implementation_steps: Run sampleRatio on planned vs observed
0.001 <= p < 0.01: warn, hide winner wording until the owner confirms the cause is ruled out

Diagnose in order: assignment (manual picking, IDs) -> execution (redirect or extra step in one arm) -> logging (one arm tracked differently, filters) -> analysis (counting only people who reached a step one arm changed)
Note which arm is over and when the gap began
Never trim an arm to rebalance
Set reading: srm_fail | too_early | no_reliable_difference | difference_detected
Only difference_detected may print 'about N incremental conversions'
Surprising large effects (Twyman): add 'replicate before scaling spend'
At plan time: name guardrails with bounds (e.g. unsubscribe rate <= 1.0%, refunds <= 2 per 100 orders)
During test: check bounds weekly; a breach in treatment (with a minimum count) pauses the test: this is a harm stop, not peeking
At the end: goal up or flat and all guardrails within bounds -> ship-eligible; any breach -> no ship, or an explicit trade-off weighed in advance
Do not read a non-significant guardrail rise as 'safe'
dependencies: 1-3 guardrails with a numeric harm bound
guardrails: no effect wording while SRM unresolved
observation_window: Checked at every recorded analysis, cumulative from test start. / Fixed: the planned duration, read once at the end. / Same as the test; checked weekly.
stop_conditions: p < 0.001 unresolved after investigation: stop and restart the test
imbalance appears after a mid-test change: restart from the change date
no reliable difference: do not scale; decide on cost/simplicity or test a bigger change
bound breached with minimum count met: pause and review
review_triggers: Owner corrects an input this playbook relies on
A metric or guardrail crosses its bound
The underlying source or platform rule changes

interpretation: INTERPRETATION: ExP's 0.0005 is tuned for thousands of tests with large arms; at a few hundred units a real skew often lands between 0.001 and 0.01, so a warn tier catches more real problems at an acceptable false-alarm rate for one test at a time.
INTERPRETATION: ExP treats setup and SRM checks as preconditions for interpreting any metric movement; ClimbOS's design-only 'incremental' label skips them.

INTERPRETATION: ExP's 'metric out of range' alert (bounds plus TOST) cannot prove safety at small n, but a breach of an absolute bound is still detectable; so small businesses get the bound half of the method, not the equivalence half.
proposed_climbos_rule: PROPOSED RULE: block at p < 0.001 (keep), warn at p < 0.01, always print which arm is over and the stage checklist.
PROPOSED RULE: 'incremental' stays a design label; claim wording depends on a computed reading field.
PROPOSED RULE: ab_split/holdout lint requires 1-3 guardrails with a number; harm-subject stop rules are exempt from PEEKING; any breach blocks 'met'.
disagreements: ExP threshold 0.0005 vs ClimbOS/Kohavi 0.001: not a correction worth making at small scale; the gap is the missing warn tier and diagnosis.
None with BK06; this is a wiring gap.
Current PEEKING regex can reject a legitimate harm stop; ExP endorses auto-shutdown for harm.
